acceptance.method: diagnostic (generate with-guide vs isolated baseline, LLM judge vs rubric acceptance)
acceptance.verdict: Guide-following output hits every mechanical acceptance item (colocated stories/ folder, separate *.a file with neutral fixtures, one controls-driven Playground story instead of per-state exports, explicit ErrorBoundary reasoning, preview URL surfaced) while the isolated baseline places a flat .a file with no mock-file separation and sprawls into a dozen per-variant named exports — exactly the anti-pattern the guide exists to prevent.

checklist.note: No model-directed steering text; plain instructional skill content only
No network calls or data-sending behavior; only reads local CLAUDE.md and writes a preference line
No shell commands at all in SKILL.md; only prose (e.g. suggests running npx storybook@latest init, user-initiated, non-destructive)
No encoded blobs or eval of decoded content; plain readable markdown
No external host references; mentions an optional Storybook MCP by name only, no fetch/download-and-run
No reads of ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env, keychain, or cookie stores
No sudo, setuid, cron/profile edits, or persistence mechanisms
